starting_principles: Rate of change of angular momentum: $\frac{d\vec{L}_O}{dt} = \vec{\tau}_O = \vec{r} \times \vec{F}$
assumptions: The particle is treated as a classical point mass $m$.
The reference point $O$ is fixed in an inertial frame.
Classical non-relativistic mechanics where mass $m$ is constant.

ordered_steps.description: Define the instantaneous position and linear momentum of a particle relative to a chosen reference origin $O$.
ordered_steps.operation: Specify the particle's mass $m$ and position vector $\vec{r}$ measured from origin $O$. Define linear momentum $\vec{p} = m \vec{v} = m \frac{d\vec{r}}{dt}$.
assumptions_applied: Classical point mass with invariant mass $m$.

ordered_steps.description: Formulate the moment of momentum (angular momentum) $\vec{L}_O$ as the vector cross product of position and linear momentum.
ordered_steps.operation: Take the vector cross product of position vector $\vec{r}$ with linear momentum $\vec{p}$: $\vec{L}_O = \vec{r} \times \vec{p} = \vec{r} \times (m \vec{v})$.
assumptions_applied: Scalar mass $m$ factors out of the cross product.

ordered_steps.description: Differentiate the angular momentum vector with respect to time to verify dynamic consistency with Newton's second law.
ordered_steps.operation: Apply the product rule of vector calculus: $\frac{d\vec{L}_O}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}(\vec{r} \times \vec{p}) = \left(\frac{d\vec{r}}{dt} \times \vec{p}\right) + \left(\vec{r} \times \frac{d\vec{p}}{dt}\right)$.
assumptions_applied: Product rule for vector cross products.

ordered_steps.description: Evaluate the first term $\vec{v} \times \vec{p}$ using the definition of linear momentum.
ordered_steps.operation: Factor out mass $m$: $\vec{v} \times (m \vec{v}) = m (\vec{v} \times \vec{v})$. Since the cross product of any vector with itself is identically zero, this term vanishes.
assumptions_applied: Collinear vectors produce zero cross product: $\vec{v} \times \vec{v} = \vec{0}$.

ordered_steps.description: Substitute Newton's second law $\frac{d\vec{p}}{dt} = \vec{F}_{\text{net}}$ into the second term to prove $\frac{d\vec{L}_O}{dt} = \vec{\tau}_O$.
ordered_steps.operation: Replace $\frac{d\vec{p}}{dt}$ with $\vec{F}_{\text{net}}$: $\frac{d\vec{L}_O}{dt} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F}_{\text{net}} = \vec{\tau}_O$, verifying foundational dynamical consistency.
assumptions_applied: Newton's second law in an inertial reference frame.

ordered_steps.description: Compute the scalar magnitude of angular momentum in terms of the impact parameter $r_\perp$.
ordered_steps.operation: Calculate magnitude: $|\vec{L}_O| = m |\vec{r}||\vec{v}|\sin\theta = m v (r \sin\theta) = m v r_\perp = p r_\perp$, where $r_\perp = r \sin\theta$ is the perpendicular distance from $O$ to the line of motion.

applicability_conditions: Applies to any point mass particle moving along an arbitrary trajectory in 3D space.
Reference point $O$ must be explicitly specified.
Valid in an inertial reference frame.
